notes: OTR for 12µm BOPET. Typical published ranges exist in literature but vary by grade, thickness, and supplier. A specific validated value for the intended grade must be obtained from the material supplier datasheet and independently verified. Prototype cannot reproduce a specific numeric value here.
WVTR for 12µm BOPET. Specific validated value requires supplier datasheet verification.
OTR for PE (LDPE ~40µm). PE has high oxygen permeability — it is a poor oxygen barrier. Qualitative classification: HIGH OTR. Specific value requires validation.
WVTR for PE. PE is a better moisture barrier than oxygen barrier. Qualitative: LOW-MEDIUM WVTR. Specific value requires validation.

OTR for MetPET. Metallised PET offers significantly improved oxygen barrier vs plain PET. Qualitative: LOW OTR. However, exact values are grade/supplier/metallisation-quality dependent. Prototype cannot assign a specific validated numeric value.
WVTR for MetPET. Improved moisture barrier vs plain PET. Specific value requires supplier datasheet validation.

OTR for solid aluminium foil (9µm). Near-zero oxygen transmission when defect-free. Qualitative: VERY LOW OTR. Actual performance affected by defects, pinholes, lamination stress. Prototype marks as NEEDS_VALIDATION — no fabricated numeric value assigned.
WVTR for solid aluminium foil. Near-zero moisture transmission when defect-free. Qualitative: VERY LOW WVTR.

OTR for cast PP film (~30µm). PP has higher oxygen permeability than PET — used in MAP applications where controlled gas exchange is needed, not barrier. Qualitative: MEDIUM-HIGH OTR. Specific value requires validation.
CO2 transmission rate for PP. CO2TR is typically 3-6x OTR for polyolefins (CO2:O2 permeability ratio). This ratio is used in MAP analysis for fresh produce. Specific validated value required.
